newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey parliament drops censure motion.
newsitem.headline: Turkey parliament drops censure motion.

text.p: Turkey's parliament voted on Tuesday not to proceed with a censure motion against the Islamist-led government, deputy speaker Hasan Korkmazcan said.
MPs voted 281 to 246 to reject two leftist bids to hold a ballot on bringing down Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's coalition for allegedly threatening Turkey's secular system, he said.
"According to this result, the proposals will not be put on the agenda," Korkmazcan said.
Erbakan, NATO member Turkey's first Islamist leader, has been under fire from secularists for a series of symbolic measures to increase the profile of Islam in public life.
The powerful armed forces have been among the strongest critics of Erbakan's coalition with pro-Western conservative Tansu Ciller.
The Milliyet newspaper on Tuesday quoted navy chief Admiral Guven Erkaya as saying he had called on the military top brass to formally warn Erbakan against Islamist militancy.
